facts.text: ALSEP Central Station was deployed at Hadley Rille during Apollo 15 in 1971.
Apollo 15's experiment suite included a heat flow experiment (drilled into the surface), a lunar dust detector, and a solar wind spectrometer. Powered by an RTG, it ran until 1977.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Its heat flow experiment measured the Moon's internal temperature gradient for the first time, and its lunar dust detector tracked the electrostatic behavior of fine particles in vacuum.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Hadley Rille.
Operated from 1971 until shutdown on 30 September 1977; the heat flow data remains critical for modeling the Moon's thermal evolution.
